approachQuestion.prompt:
A common calibration instant

All n instruments must be calibrated at one common instant. Instrument i is available during a closed interval [start,end]. Return the entire closed interval of instants when all instruments are available, or null if none exists. A one-point answer is valid. The input is unsorted and immutable.

Input: availability=[[1,9],[3,7],[5,8]]
Output: [5,7]

Input: availability=[[1,4],[4,6],[2,5]]
Output: [4,4]

Input: availability=[[0,2],[3,5]]
Output: null

Constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; integer endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ start ≤ end ≤ 1000000000. Return only one pair or null. Choose the best worst-case time, then least auxiliary memory.

options.text: Scan once for the largest start and smallest end. Return that pair if largestStart ≤ smallestEnd, otherwise null.
options.feedback: A time must be no earlier than every start and no later than every end. These two extremal constraints are both necessary and sufficient, including equality.

options.text: Copy all starts and all ends into separate arrays, sort them, and compare the greatest start with the smallest end.
options.feedback: This returns the correct common interval for every input and identifies the right boundaries. Sorting and storing every endpoint are unnecessary when only two extrema are required.

options.text: Return [smallestStart,largestEnd] when any two intervals overlap.
options.feedback: For [[1,9],[3,7],[5,8]], the common interval is [5,7], not [1,9]. Union boundaries do not describe instants available to every instrument.

options.text: Find the largest start and smallest end, but return null when they are equal.
options.feedback: For [[1,4],[4,6]], instant 4 belongs to both closed intervals, so [4,4] is required. Equality is not emptiness here.

feedback.reason: Reduce a global simultaneous intersection to two necessary and sufficient extremal bounds.
details: Initialize the largest start and smallest end from the first interval. Scan remaining intervals, update these two values, then return their pair if ordered, or null. Do not sort or copy the input.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For max-start-min-end, n is the number of instruments. Count temporary state, excluding the input and returned pair or null. Choose the tightest standard worst-case pair.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)

feedback.reason: Inspect every interval once using two extreme endpoint values.
details: Each interval can tighten an extreme, requiring a linear scan in the worst case. Two endpoint values and a loop index are constant auxiliary state. Sorting would add work and memory; merely reading the first interval cannot determine all constraints.
Iterative scan of n≥1 closed intervals; no temporary arrays.
“Time O(n log n), auxiliary space O(n)”: Only extrema are needed, so this method neither sorts nor stores all endpoints. It scans once using scalar state.
“Time O(n), auxiliary space O(n)”: No temporary array is allocated. Two boundary extrema and the loop index use constant auxiliary memory.
“Time O(1), auxiliary space O(1)”: Any instrument can tighten the bounds or eliminate the intersection. Inspecting all n inputs is necessary in the worst case.
